title: C1184 — Fuel injector 4 connector
introduction:
An injector is an electrically controlled valve that meters fuel. I read this reference as its electrical address book: the housing drawing helps identify the connection, and the circuit rows explain where its connections belong. A familiar-looking plug alone does not tell the whole story.

Start with the identity table, follow the printed cavity labels into the assignment table, then use the pigtail listing to distinguish the connector shell from the catalogued service assembly. The driver connection and supply connection have different descriptions; keep each description attached to its own row.

This page teaches reference reading. Physical viewing direction, access, test conditions and replacement methods require matching vehicle documentation. Engine applicability and the Gauge, Size and Used conventions are unspecified here, so these entries do not establish injection type or repair-wire selection.

edits.why: The illustration shows vertically stacked cavities beneath the latch. I use those features to navigate the drawing, then follow the printed cavity labels into the table. The identity details and shell-and-harness row keep the drawing tied to the named connector. This printed arrangement does not establish a terminal-side or wire-side viewing direction for a physical connector.

Read across the row matching the drawing’s cavity label. Circuit Number identifies the circuit, Color describes its wire, and Function distinguishes the injector-driver connection from the supply connection. Preserve the supply description’s fuse or circuit-breaker alternatives; this reference does not select between them. The driver entry’s polarity sign remains part of its label and does not establish switching behavior or a test voltage.

Follow Kit List in the identity table to Number in this listing. Service Part identifies the catalogued pigtail assembly, while Engineering Shell connects that listing to the housing identification above. Terminal Part Number in the assignment table refers to a different item. Keep the circuit-wire and pigtail Gauge entries separate; the listing is useful identification evidence, not a splice or replacement procedure.
